findings.rule: correctness: undeclared name in a feature-macro path
findings.why: With MEMORY_VERIFICATION_ENABLED=1 this names a member that does not exist (the storage is `block`), so 10 of 12 Memory translation units stop compiling - measured. It also masks every other profile/verification path in the module, including the ones this commit rewrote.
findings.fix: rename the argument to `block` (sizeof(block) equals `length`), then add a `-DPROFILE_ENABLED=1 -DMEMORY_VERIFICATION_ENABLED=1` syntax-only layer to the gate so these paths stop being unverified.

findings.rule: docs: API-reference pointer resolves to nothing
findings.why: docs/Memory/PoolAllocator/index.html does not exist; comments.py reports POINTER-PATH. The commit deleted the @brief block and installed an address to a page that was never authored, which the standard forbids: an entry without a page carries no pointer.
findings.fix: author the page with .pi/skills/hb-docs/scripts/docs_page.py, or remove the pointer line until the page exists.

findings.rule: correctness: null pointer used after a failed allocation
findings.why: The added Assert(ptr != nullptr, ...) is compiled away in Release, where Assert is a no-op, so the placement-new on the next line still constructs through a null pointer. The same commit fixed exactly this class in Allocate/Deallocate with an early return.
findings.fix: if (ptr == nullptr) { Assert(false, ...); return nullptr; } - assert in debug, fail the call in release.

findings.rule: correctness: null pointer used after a failed allocation
findings.why: The added Assert(buffer != nullptr, ...) does not stop anything in Release; the next line forms an address from a null pointer and the loop after it writes a free list through it.
findings.fix: make the pool inert on failure (buffer stays null, numberOfBlocks = 0) or FatalAssert and document the policy; an assert alone is a debug-only guard.

findings.rule: policy: an unreleased-build-only assert now aborts in release
findings.why: FatalAssert is declared outside the !RELEASE_BUILD block (Debug.h:74, :89), so it aborts in every configuration; an invalid allocator id used to log and return a dummy proxy and now aborts a Release process too. The retained 'static AllocatorProxy dummy{}; return dummy;' is not a defect: 42 of 75 FatalAssert call sites are followed by a return, and keeping it makes the code correct whichever policy FatalAssert follows. Only the choice itself is unrecorded.
findings.fix: Owner ruling: keep the return. Do not add [[noreturn]] to FatalAssert - if it ever becomes a Release no-op, returning to a caller whose tail was deleted as unreachable is undefined behaviour. If Release is meant to survive the call, move the FatalAssert definitions into the !RELEASE_BUILD block; either way, say which policy the entry owns.

findings.rule: correctness: profiler records a failed allocation
findings.why: AllocateBlock returns nullptr when the pool is exhausted and the profiling branch reports it anyway, so stats.usage grows for an allocation that never happened. The commit guarded the mirror-image underflow in ReportDeallocation but left its source.
findings.fix: report only when ptr != nullptr.

findings.rule: test: assertion that cannot fail
findings.why: peakBlocks sums bank.GetUsedBlocksMax() over every bank and reportedBlocks sums the same per-bank values accumulated one entry per size class, so the two are equal by construction. The assert proves a property of its own accumulation loop, not of the allocator, and its message over-claims.
findings.fix: compare against an independently derived figure (a snapshot of the per-bank peak taken before the lock, or a per-size-class recomputation), or delete the assert and keep the rename.
findings.evidence: Assert(reportedBlocks == peakBlocks, "ReportConfiguration: the reported block count ", reportedBlocks,

findings.rule: architecture: external linkage for a file-local type
findings.why: BankGenerationLog (and BankUsageRecord further down) are defined at namespace scope inside a .cpp without an anonymous namespace, so they have external linkage and can collide with the same name in another translation unit - an ODR hazard the engine's no-namespace-indent style makes easy to repeat.
findings.fix: wrap both in `namespace { ... }` (or make them private nested types) and declare them together instead of one at the top and one mid-file.

findings.rule: performance: per-allocation cost for a log line
findings.why: A thread-local pointer write plus five stores happen on every Allocate, but the log fires only when a bank is generated. Single-thread Allocate is ~24 ns in this commit's own M1 measurement, so the overhead is a real fraction of the operation it is meant to describe.
findings.fix: construct the scope object in NewBankAllocate (the only path that records) or skip construction when the logger would not emit Verbose.

findings.rule: docs: an undeclared locking invariant
findings.why: GenerateBank locks nothing and sorts `banks` in place; it is only correct because every caller holds `lock`. Engine sources cannot carry that note and no design document was added, so the invariant lives nowhere: a later edit that adds a lock inside it self-deadlocks a non-recursive std::mutex.
findings.fix: add docs/Memory/ThreadSafeMultiPoolAllocator design notes recording the caller-must-hold-lock rule, the deferred-logging protocol and why banks are sorted under the lock.

findings.rule: test: regression test cannot detect its own bug
findings.why: The testlet is named for where the pool buffer must go, but it only checks that an allocation succeeded; it never observes which allocator received the buffer, so the pre-fix behaviour (buffer returned to the ambient scope) still passes.
findings.fix: measure the destination: use MemoryManager::GetGlobalAllocationBytes/GetGlobalFreeBytes deltas like the StackAllocator and MonotonicAllocator testlets, or assert the unrelated allocator's usage stays 0.
findings.evidence: ls << "The pool handed out no block, so its buffer was never exercised." << lferr;

findings.rule: test: invariant checked against the wrong modulus
findings.why: The free loop reduces modulo slots.size(), which is numThreads * ContentionOpsPerThread, not ContentionOpsPerThread. The assert passes today only because the resolved thread counts are 1, 2, 4 and 8; a count that shares a factor with the stride makes the loop free some slots twice and leak others.
findings.fix: verify the permutation at run time (build the index order once and assert it is a bijection) or free through a shuffled order built with a fixed seed.

findings.rule: test: unchecked allocation result, then a dealloc with a size
findings.why: A null result is stored and later passed to Deallocate with a non-zero size, which now logs a Warning and reaches Assert(size == 0). In a non-Release build one failed allocation aborts the whole EngineTest process instead of reporting one failed testlet.
findings.fix: record a null count, skip the matching free, and report it as a testlet failure.

findings.rule: test: a worker exception aborts the whole suite
findings.why: An exception escaping a worker reaches std::terminate and takes the test binary with it; the timeout path then joins a thread that will never finish. One allocator fault becomes a suite-wide loss of evidence.
findings.fix: catch inside the worker lambda, store the failure in ContentionWorkerRecord and report it as a testlet failure.

findings.rule: redundancy: the same testlet written three times
findings.why: The Destroy In Own Scope testlet in StackAllocator.cpp, MonotonicAllocator.cpp and InlineMonotonicAllocator.cpp are near-identical (same parent registration, same byte-delta comparison, same message shape). Three copies drift independently, which is the failure this project's standards cycle removes on sight.
findings.fix: hoist one helper (e.g. TestCollection::ReportRetainedBytesOnDestroy) and call it from the three collections.

findings.rule: policy: unsigned <= 0 kept on purpose (house style)
findings.why: House style, ruled blanket by the owner: an unsigned `x <= 0` is written on purpose, so the negative case is already handled if the value is later revised to a signed integer. Closed as a decision, not a defect. `len` is `data.size()` today, so the guard only ever means `== 0`.
findings.fix: None - no code change requested or made; kept in the record so the next reviewer does not re-report it. Measured cost under this build: nil - clang++ -std=gnu++23 -Wall -Werror is silent on this shape, and -Wtautological-compare / -Weverything emit no diagnostic either (clang warns on `unsigned >= 0`, not `<= 0`). GCC's -Wtype-limits, enabled by -Wall, does warn on it, which is the price if a GCC build is ever configured. No checker greps for `<= 0`, so no waiver mechanism is needed.

findings.rule: observability: leak report lost in release
findings.why: The replaced code logged a Warning and debugBreak in every configuration; Assert prints nothing in Release, so an allocator that leaks at deregistration is now silent in the shipped configuration. The old early `return` also became fall-through, so the stats entry is now removed where it used to be kept - two silent behaviour changes inside a commit sold as fixes.
findings.fix: keep the Log(Warning) and add the Assert, and state the new control flow in the class page.

findings.rule: architecture: unconstrained constructor template
findings.why: The constructor template accepts anything and calls allocator.GetID() on it, so a wrong argument is diagnosed inside the constructor rather than at the call site. The commit tightened the two non-template overloads with explicit but left this one open.
findings.fix: constrain it with a concept (requires { allocator.GetID(); } -> TAllocatorID) or drop it in favour of the ID overload at call sites.

findings.rule: architecture: an allocator that owns an id does not forbid copying
findings.why: MultiPoolAllocator and ThreadSafeMultiPoolAllocator register an allocator id and hold raw backing pointers, yet declare no deleted or defaulted copy/move operations; they are non-copyable only by accident of an HVector member. The proxy-aliasing bug this commit fixed in PoolAllocator returns the day anyone adds a move constructor here and forgets to repoint allocProxy.allocator.
findings.fix: state it explicitly: `MultiPoolAllocator(const MultiPoolAllocator&) = delete;` and the move deleted (or declared with the proxy repointed, mirroring PoolAllocator).

findings.rule: correctness: no self-move guard
findings.why: The implementation destroys *this and then placement-news from rhs; on self-assignment it constructs from an object it just destroyed. Pre-existing, but it is the file whose move semantics this commit had to repair.
findings.fix: add `if (this == &rhs) { return *this; }`, or make the move-assign destroy rhs after releasing this.

findings.rule: tooling: a checker that no gate runs
findings.why: quoted_blocks.py is 625 new lines and SKILL.md documents it as an exit-code gate, but no script invokes it - it appears only in SKILL.md, and check.sh at the reviewed commit never mentions it. Run by hand it already reports 1 stale and 1 unresolved block in docs/Container, so it works and its findings are currently nobody's job.
findings.fix: invoke it from check.sh layer 5 beside htmlcheck.py, or state in SKILL.md that it is manual and name who runs it.

findings.why: clang-format wants a space after the comment marker. This spelling sits in 104 files, so check.sh layer 1 is red tree-wide. It came from the macro-rename commit rather than the allocator commit, and it is one mechanical edit away.
